scope: Read-only, pinned, bounded source inspection through GitHub connector; not an exhaustive historical literature search.

findings.finding: Coordinate-only S3 quotient/Horner/norm/GCD elimination, exceptional leading-coefficient branches, exact candidate recovery, and capped root splitting already exist. The file also has S4 pair-support and division-free factorized resultant variants. These are related prior elimination; polynomial elimination by itself is not a new contribution.
findings.scope_boundary: The m2 oracle solves two decomposition summands for a known target. Its per-target cost does not solve selection from a third random pool for free. The checked m2 port is separately scoped; the full m3 control scans targets and charges every tried target. Existing m4 routines were source-inspected, not replayed.

findings.finding: Bounded random mixed-label single-relation experiments already construct Ri=alpha_i*G+beta_i*Q without the target log, perform coordinate-domain solving, enumerate signs, skip uninformative B=0 relations, and verify dG=Q. Exact-domain F4, hybrid guessing, separating colorings, and curve automorphism label propagation are present.
findings.implication: The labelled-pool model and one-informative-relation recovery are controls and prior art, not novel features of the new incidence selector.

findings.finding: The native m3 meet-in-the-middle pair table builds x(Fj+Fk) and x(Fj-Fk) with one batched inversion per row and x-only additions, retaining witness/sign information. It has B^2 16-byte entries. The local C++ control faithfully uses that arithmetic pattern but streams two independent pools into an O(B) third-pool index.
findings.implication: A strong O(B^2) pair control is required. This standalone C++ implementation is a portable algorithm-level control; its times are not times from the original Rust binary.

findings.finding: The deterministic prime31 curve and Dickson fiber Base::build supply the replayed B31 and B135 m2 cases. The compact structured base has no mixed labels supplied by its compact coordinate construction.
findings.implication: The structured-base correctness replay is separate from naturally sampled mixed-labelled pools. No free combination of their advantages is claimed.

findings.finding: The inspected native C index-calculus implementation explicitly targets the multiplicative group (Z/pZ)* for p<2^64. It is not an ECDLP incidence/GCD control and its timings are not compared against elliptic-curve algorithms.
The bounded rational reconstruction helper is for native multiplicative-group index-calculus descent; it does not provide the missing prime-field elliptic-curve relation selector.

The elliptic-curve section explicitly distinguishes full-pipeline data from one-residual oracle diagnostics, cites crypto's boundary ledger and residual-walk notes, and reports no complete prime-field ECDLP advantage over matched rho in its measured cells.
findings.scope_boundary: These are the repository authors' recorded conclusions, not independently replayed native timings here. The cross-reference to crypto is not an independent second experiment.

provenance: source_provenance.json records all 8 exact source blobs, pinned commit URLs, verified Git blob hashes and SHA256 capture hashes.
implementation_boundary: cargo/rustc were unavailable; no exact native Rust replay was performed. The m2 Python-FLINT port and C++ pair arithmetic are independently checked portable implementations.
